title: adaptive prefill prober and fragmented-KV reconciliation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Paged attention and fragmented KV caches are a major source of decode tail latency at high concurrency. We routinely see stalls from scattered fragment reads and repeated small prefill reads that miss because the fragment is split across non-contiguous pages. Existing allocation heuristics focus on LRU-style aging and slab compaction windows, but they do not proactively probe upcoming request patterns to bias allocations toward contiguous residency for hot token spans.

Goal:
Design, implement, and validate an "Adaptive Prefill Prober" plus a lightweight "Fragment Reconciliation" stage that together reduce p99 decode latency by improving prefill hit rates and reducing cross-page reads. The prober will issue low-cost sampling prefetches to estimate span locality and kernel-friendliness; the reconciliation will compact high-value fragmented entries into contiguous buckets when beneficial.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- +10-20% increase in prefill/KV hit-rate on representative workloads (conversational + long-context pipelines)
- p99 decode latency reduction >= 8ms on canary hosts under 95th percentile load profile
- no more than 5% additional token-serving CPU overhead in steady-state sampling mode
- fragmentation score (defined below) reduced by >= 30% on warm caches

Design overview:
1) Adaptive Prefill Prober
   - For inbound requests, maintain a lightweight per-model "span heat sketch": a small count-min like structure and a recency window of token-span fingerprints (not full keys) used purely for locality estimation.
   - On admission of a request, choose up to N small probe reads (N configurable, default 1-2) targeted at predictive offsets calculated from last-k tokens and the heat sketch. Probes are low-priority I/O that do not block decode but populate an admission score per fragment.
   - The prober combines: recent sequence-length histogram, request-level predicted continuation length, and fragment contiguity estimate to produce a "contiguity score" used by the allocator and kernel selector.

2) Fragment Reconciliation
   - Periodic opportunistic compaction job that runs across KV shard partitions. It considers fragments with: high contiguity score, high touch frequency, and a fragmentation entropy metric (how many pages a logical token-span maps to).
   - If moving a fragment to contiguous pages reduces expected cross-page reads (based on heat sketch) by a threshold and the cost (copy, temporary increased bandwidth) is under a budget, reconciliation will relocate and update page mappings atomically with writeback-safe pointers.
   - Avoids large-scale defrag; target is micro-rehoming (1-3 pages) for hot spans. This keeps GC and eviction pressure low while improving kernel-friendly layout.

3) Kernel selection integration
   - Kernel scoring augmented with contiguity score + sequence distribution: prefer kernels that optimize for contiguous KV fetches (block-read kernels) when contiguity score high. For low contiguity, prefer stride-friendly kernels and increase tolerance for streaming prefetch.
   - Expose an API for kernel hints from the prober so the runtime can adapt decode batch sizing and prefill window lengths per-request.

Instrumentation and metrics:
- Prefill hit rate (per-model, per-shard)
- Fragmentation entropy: for each logical span compute log(number_of_pages) weighted by touch frequency -> fragmentation_score
- Contiguity score histogram (0..1)
- Reconciliation churn (pages moved / hour) and CPU/IO cost of reconciliation jobs
- p50/p95/p99 decode latency (token generation); token-level CPU and I/O per request
- Kernel selection distribution and exec-time breakdown

Simulation and validation plan:
- Implement a simulator that replays real request traces (chat + long context streams) and models page layouts, probe behavior, and reconciliation actions. Use traces from QA and two production anonymized tenant traces (already sanitized).
- Run microbench comparisons: baseline allocator v1 (current), heuristic compactor v2, and the new prober+reconciler. Measure hit-rate, fragmentation score, and simulated latency cost (IO + compute).

Rollout plan:
1) Lab simulation and unit tests (2 weeks)
2) Internal canary on a small dedicated fleet (runtime-1.23/canary) with probes disabled (observe scoring only) to validate estimators and cost model (1 week)
3) Enable sampling probes at 0.1x (rare) across a control cluster and measure additional CPU/IO (1 week)
4) Enable reconciliation in conservative mode (budget=small) to 5% of hosts, evaluate effects (2 weeks)
5) Gradual ramp to 25%/50%/100% with monitoring and rollback hooks.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Probing overhead: Probes add I/O; we mitigate by throttling rate and prioritizing low-impact reads.
- Thundering compaction: reconciliation could cause transient I/O spikes. We'll limit concurrent reconciliation per shard and use token-bucket budgets.
- Inaccurate heat sketch estimates may mis-prioritize fragments. We'll keep prober conservative and provide feedback loop (reconciliation reversibility) for a short window.

Testing and observability:
- End-to-end E2E experiments comparing generation latency and token costs on representative workloads.
- Add dashboards in Console: prefill hit rate by model, reconciliation cost, fragmentation score, kernel-choice heatmap.
- Add per-request trace hooks to attribute slow reads to cross-page fetches vs decode time.

Open design questions:
- Optimal default probe budget (1 vs 2 probes per request) — simulation will pick; prefer safe default 1.
- Reconciliation trigger thresholds: tuneable via runtime flags and adaptive to global load.
- Whether to persist contiguity score in shard metadata for warm-start across restarts.

Related work / links:
- Reference allocator notes: Confluence link (internal) - https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime/paged-attn-allocator (placeholder)
- Trace samples (sanitized) - drive/redwood/traces/2025/q1-prefill-samples
- Related tickets: ENG-272459 (prefill-decoupled-kernel-routing), ENG-314159 (epochal-slab-tiering-prefill-synchronizer) — used as dependency anchors for simulation inputs

Implementation checklist:
- [ ] heat sketch proto and API (fast increment/read)
- [ ] prober admission hooks and low-priority probe queue
- [ ] contiguity score calculation and exposure to allocator & kernel selector
- [ ] compact (reconcile) worker with safe atomic page remap
- [ ] instrumentation + dashboards + alerts
- [ ] simulation harness and regression tests
comments: 2025-03-11 - Initial design doc drafted by Aisha. Proposed heat-sketch is intentionally tiny to keep mem overhead low.
2025-03-12 - Architecture sync: Marco + Priya + Lukas. Agreed to build prober as non-blocking low-priority operation. Priya suggested adding a small decay to contiguity scores to avoid oscillation.

2025-03-14 - Simulation prototype results: with conservative reconciliation budget we see +12% prefill hit-rate and p99 decode down 6.5ms in sim. CPU overhead ~2.8% in hotspots. Action: tighten reconciliation gating and rerun with alternate trace.
2025-03-16 - Design review with runtime team. Feedback: ensure kernel hint API is minimal (3 fields: contiguity_score, expected_continuation_len, probe_confidence). Marco to draft API in PR.
2025-03-18 - Bench notes: small canary (disabled probes) shows contiguity score distribution aligned with sim. Agreed to start sample-probes at 0.05 rate on canary hosts next week.
